title: Second-hand smoke from neighbours' homes: complaints, resolution and possible new measures
asked: Mr Liang Eng Hwa asked how many complaints NEA received in 2025 about second-hand smoke from neighbours smoking in their own homes, how many were amicably resolved, and what new measures NEA is considering to resolve such disputes.
response: NEA received about 600 cases of feedback in 2025 on second-hand tobacco smoke from neighbouring homes, and about 30% of those came from repeat feedback providers. NEA works with other agencies or the relevant Town Council to issue advisories to surrounding units, does not track whether cases are amicably resolved, and says most feedback cases did not recur after advisories; unresolved cases may lead to in-person engagement, and residents are encouraged to try mediation such as the Community Mediation Centre. Dr Janil said the ministry can continue to explore mechanisms and step up messaging, noting there are now about 49,000 no-smoking spaces islandwide, and that it can work with the Health Promotion Board on public health messages and HDB on responsible neighbour behaviour.

left_open: Whether second-hand smoke coming from neighbours' windows and balconies will be classified as a public nuisance under the Environmental Public Health Act
Whether smoking at windows and balconies will be added to HDB's good-neighbour handbook or otherwise given clearer public messaging
supplementary: The MP pressed for classifying second-hand smoke from homes as public nuisance and for stronger public messaging on smoking at windows and balconies.
